Let $\mathcal P$ be a pi-system generating $\mathcal A$, with an increasing sequence $P_n\in\mathcal P$ covering $X$ and satisfying $\mu(P_n)<\infty$. F6 therefore extends equality of cylinder probabilities to all product-measurable sets, proving measure preservation.. Exact source excerpt and inputs are retained in the owned proof contract. Step-5 author dependency check against current items/def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system.md, Definition. Required supplier statement: Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space. A measurable self-map $T:X\to X$ is **measure preserving** if $\mu(T^{-1}E)=\mu(E)$ for every $E\in\mathcal A$. The quadruple $(X,\mathcal A,\mu,T)$ is a **measure-preserving system**; it is a probability system if $\mu(X)=1$. Here $T^{-1}E=\{x:T(x)\in E\}$ denotes an inverse image, whether or not $T$ is invertible. Neither completeness nor finiteness is implicit. The measure-space and measurable-map conventions are [[def-measure-space]] and [[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]. Actual use in items/lem-finite-probability-maximal-ergodic-inequality.md: step 1.1: The measurable self-map in F1 and F2 make all finite sums and maxima measurable. Also $0\le M_N\le\sum_{j<N}|f|\circ T^j$, whose integral is $N\int|f|\,dP<\infty$ by F3. Thus M_N and its composition with T are integrable.. Exact source excerpt and inputs are retained in the owned proof contract. This records the consumer interface check, not independent adjudication.
